request.what: Reduce the Cardano committeeMinSize protocol parameter from 7 to 5.

claims.claim: The proposal changes only the minimum Constitutional Committee size parameter, committeeMinSize, from 7 to 5.
The current Constitutional Committee has 7 members, equal to the current committeeMinSize of 7.
A single resignation or term expiration under the current setting could make governance actions requiring Constitutional Committee approval ineligible for ratification.
Reducing committeeMinSize to 5 would create an operational buffer allowing governance to continue if one or two members retire or terms expire, assuming a current 7-member body.
The proposal says the action depends temporally on another live Plutus cost model parameter-change action and has no technical interaction with it.
Intersect states the submission was approved by the Civics Committee on 2026-03-13 and by the Technical Steering Committee on 2026-06-03.
The proposer states the change has undergone technical review through the Parameter Committee Parameter Change Process and references the Cardano Forum PCP-005 discussion.
The proposal states that setting committeeMinSize to 5 satisfies the listed guardrails that it must be non-negative, not lower than 3, and not exceed 10.
The proposal acknowledges that with a 5-member Constitutional Committee and a 2/3 threshold, one inactive member would allow another member to fully veto governance actions.

The proposal says reversion to committeeMinSize 7 is possible if there are at least 7 Constitutional Committee members, but would halt governance immediately if fewer than 7 members existed at reversion time.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury parameter change reducing committeeMinSize from 7 to 5 to improve governance operational resilience, while acknowledging altered veto dynamics at smaller committee sizes and providing references to committee approvals, PCP review, and a reversion plan.
